findings.finding: The new note says Rosemary Morris "says the same", meaning that the Great Lavra was founded by Nicephorus Phocas. The repo does not show Morris saying that. It cites her on the movement only as a study of "patrons, property, holy men". It also lists her among the sources of a story whose own text (marked 'from reference summaries; primary text not yet read') says Athanasios built the Lavra with Phokas's gold. That supports Phocas as patron, which is enough for the ruling-1 upgrade. It does not support attributing the words 'founded by Phocas' to Morris. Keep the grade but stop putting that claim in her mouth.
findings.evidence: census movement athonite-and-comnenian-byzantine-monasticism, sources: "Rosemary Morris, Monks and Laymen in Byzantium, 843-1118 (CUP, 1995)", "note": "Standard study of the monastic world's social ecosystem: patrons, property, holy men."; story 'The Founder Killed by His Own Church' text: "been persuaded by his friend the general Nikephoros Phokas to build a communal monastery there, and when Phokas became emperor had accepted his gold to do it"; edge note: "But Rosemary Morris, a modern scholar, says the same in a book of 1995."
findings.required_fix: note = "Robert Curzon was an English visitor to Athos in the 1830s. He cites an account from 1701: the Great Lavra 'was founded by Nicephorus Phocas', the emperor. That report is late and secondhand. But a modern study by Rosemary Morris, from 1995, tells how Phocas paid for the house that the monk Athanasios built."
